title: Reject white-glove retention plans that violate self-serve and auditability constraints

problem_spec.request: Find the best retention strategy for a workflow-heavy B2B product that wants a stronger moat without becoming enterprise-only.
constraints: Stay self-serve for teams under 50 seats.
Keep every recommendation auditable from stored artifacts.
success_criteria: Increase repeated weekly use by team leads.
Create a retention mechanism that gets stronger as real work accumulates.

candidate.thesis: Deliver a high-touch retention consulting layer
candidate.mechanism: Assign a customer-success strategist to configure each team's workflow, review usage every week, and hand-build executive recaps that persuade leadership to renew.
assumptions: Teams will accept a services-heavy rollout if the strategic advice feels premium.
strengths: Can produce tailored guidance for each account.
failure_modes: Requires manual setup and recurring analyst labor.
unknowns: Can the product retain teams once the human consultant steps back?
candidate.implementation_shape: Pilot with customer-success pods and bespoke reporting playbooks.
evidence: The idea could improve retention for a few high-touch accounts, but only through services.

hard_constraint_reasons: Depends on sales-assisted onboarding instead of a self-serve motion.
Relies on bespoke human reporting rather than auditable product artifacts.

expected_assessment.summary: The plan is concrete, but it fails the self-serve and auditability requirements that define the actual product brief.
weaknesses: Produces service output instead of durable product artifacts.
open_questions: Is there any version of the retention insight that can be productized without human operators?
